concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: In which year the Nawab of Awadh was forced to give over half of his territory to the East India Company?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1801**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the year **1801**, the **Nawab of Awadh**, under pressure from the **East India Company**, was forced to cede more than half of his territory to the British.
 
• This agreement was part of the **Subsidiary Alliance system**, initiated by **Lord Wellesley**, the then Governor-General of India.
 
• The ceded territories included fertile and strategically significant regions such as **Rohilkhand, the Doab region, and Gorakhpur**.
 
• The Nawab was also required to disband his army and allow a British contingent to be stationed in Awadh, further ensuring British control over the region.
 
• This marked a significant step in the British consolidation of power in northern India, paving the way for further territorial expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Subsidiary Alliance System:**

 
 
• It was introduced by **Lord Wellesley** to bring Indian princely states under British control without direct annexation.
 
• Under this system, Indian rulers were required to station a British force in their territory and pay for its maintenance.
 
• The princely states could not ally with any other power or declare war without British permission, effectively reducing them to vassal states.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for the Cession of Awadh:**
 
 
• The British cited the **weak governance** of the Nawab and the need for administrative reforms as justification for taking over Awadh's territories.
 
• The fertile lands of Awadh were crucial for **agricultural production** and revenue generation for the East India Company.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Agreement:**
 
 
• The cession of territory weakened the **sovereignty** of the Nawab of Awadh, making him dependent on the British.
 
• The people of Awadh faced increased revenue demands and administrative changes under British rule.
 
• This event marked the beginning of a series of British interventions in Awadh, culminating in its complete annexation in **1856**.
 
 
 
• **Important Figures:**
 
 
• **Nawab Saadat Ali Khan II:** The Nawab of Awadh during the cession of territory in 1801.
 
• **Lord Wellesley:** Governor-General of India (1798–1805) who implemented the Subsidiary Alliance system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **East India Company's Expansion:**

 
 
• By the early 19th century, the East India Company had expanded its control over large parts of India through a combination of treaties, alliances, and military conquests.
 
• The Subsidiary Alliance system was a key tool in this expansion, allowing the British to dominate Indian states without direct administration initially.
 
 
 
• **Economic Exploitation:**
 
 
• The territories ceded by Awadh were rich in resources and played a crucial role in bolstering the Company's revenues.
 
• However, the increased revenue demands placed a significant burden on the local population, leading to widespread discontent.
 
 
 
• **Annexation of Awadh (1856):**
 
 
• In 1856, the British annexed Awadh entirely, citing **misgovernance** and the Doctrine of Lapse.
 
• This annexation was one of the factors leading to the **Revolt of 1857**, as it caused widespread resentment among the people of Awadh.
